steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The welfare state (1945): based on Beveridge Report (1942) which identified five 'giant evils': Want, Disease, Ignorance, Squalor, Idleness. Key services: NHS, state education, social security, council housing.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Universal vs means-tested benefits: universal (available to all - NHS, state education) vs means-tested (only for those below a certain income - Universal Credit). Means-testing targets resources but creates the poverty trap.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: New Right critique (Murray): welfare creates a 'dependency culture' where people rely on benefits. The 'underclass' is trapped in welfare dependency. Evaluation: 68% of families in poverty have at least one working adult; most benefit claimants are there temporarily.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Marxist view: welfare maintains capitalism (reserve army of labour, legitimises the system, controls the poor through conditionality and sanctions).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe the key features of the welfare state and evaluate different views on its role. | Evaluate the New Right view that welfare creates a dependency culture. | Assess whether poverty is caused by structural factors or individual behaviour.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Beveridge's 5 evils: Want, Disease, Ignorance, Squalor, Idleness. Welfare = NHS + education + social security + housing. New Right: DEPENDENCY CULTURE (Murray). Counter: 68% of poor families have someone WORKING. Poverty: STRUCTURAL (low wages, unemployment) > INDIVIDUAL (poor choices). Structural solutions work better.
